diagram_name: Who Made a Greek Book in Venice?
chapter_title: Day 9, Part 2: Venetian Heraklion and Crete Today
learning_objective: The learner will attribute ten contributions to Greek and humanist printing in Venice around 1500 to the people who made them, attributing at least 8 of 10 correctly on the first attempt.

Type: graph-model **sim-id:** greek-book-makers-venice-network

**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Analyze

**Learning Objective:** The learner will attribute ten contributions to Greek and humanist printing in Venice around 1500 to the people who made them, attributing at least 8 of 10 correctly on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Aldus Manutius, Marcus Musurus, Janus Lascaris, Andrea Torresani, Francesco Griffo, Zacharias Kallierges, Nikolaos Vlastos, Erasmus, Pietro Bembo, Pope Leo X, Aldine editions, collation and emendation (all defined in Part Two above). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of ten contribution cards, the learner chooses one of the ten people before feedback. A choice is correct when it matches the Correct person column in Content. Mastery is 8 of 10 correct on the first attempt. After the ten cards, the learner answers one question: "How many of the ten were born on Crete?" (correct: 3). Clicking nodes to read infoboxes after answering is exploration. **Misconceptions:** (1) Aldus did all the work himself, so every card belongs to him. (2) The editor and the printer were the same person. (3) Venice's Greek printing was Italian work, with no Greek or Cretan makers (cards 1, 6, 7). (4) A rival press was an enemy of learning rather than another route to it (cards 6 and 7). **Instructional Rationale:** Attributing each contribution to its maker forces the learner to break "the Aldine Press" into its roles (editor, publisher, type cutter, financier, teacher, author, patron), which is Analyze-level work. Building the network one confirmed link at a time makes the team, and the Cretan share in it, visible. **Content:** The ten people, shown as unconnected nodes with name and dates only: Aldus Manutius (about 1450–1515); Marcus Musurus (about 1470–1517); Janus Lascaris (about 1445–1535); Andrea Torresani (1451–1529); Francesco Griffo (about 1450–1518); Zacharias Kallierges (active about 1499–1523); Nikolaos Vlastos (active about 1499); Erasmus (about 1466–1536); Pietro Bembo (1470–1547); Pope Leo X (1475–1521). | # | Contribution card | Correct person | Reason shown after answering | Link drawn when correct | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Compared manuscripts and corrected the Greek text for the first printed Plato, 1513, and wrote a Greek poem to open it | Marcus Musurus | The Cretan editor did the scholarly work; the printer did not. | Musurus – Aldus: "edited for" | | 2 | Ran the press, chose the books, and began the small octavo classics in 1501 | Aldus Manutius | Choosing the list and the format was the publisher's work. | none (Aldus is the hub) | | 3 | Cut the punches for the italic type and for Greek types | Francesco Griffo | The punchcutter made the letters; Aldus commissioned them. | Griffo – Aldus: "cut type for" | | 4 | Put money into the press as Aldus's partner, and became his father-in-law | Andrea Torresani | A press needed capital before it sold a single book. | Torresani – Aldus: "financed" | | 5 | Taught Greek to the young Musurus in Florence | Janus Lascaris | Editors were trained by an earlier generation of Greek teachers. | Lascaris – Musurus: "taught" | | 6 | Printed the *Etymologicum Magnum*, a huge Greek dictionary, at his own press in Venice in 1499 | Zacharias Kallierges | A Cretan printer ran a Greek press of his own, separate from Aldus's. | Kallierges – Vlastos: "printed for" | | 7 | Paid for that 1499 dictionary | Nikolaos Vlastos | A Cretan merchant financed the Cretan press, as Torresani financed Aldus's. | (drawn with card 6) | | 8 | Lived in Aldus's house in 1508 while the press printed his collection of proverbs, the *Adagia* | Erasmus | The author came to the press, which shows how central it was. | Erasmus – Aldus: "printed by" | | 9 | Edited Petrarch and Dante for Aldus's small Italian editions | Pietro Bembo | The octavo format served Italian classics as well as Greek and Latin ones. | Bembo – Aldus: "edited for" | | 10 | Received the dedication of the 1513 Plato, and in 1516 called its editor to Rome as an archbishop | Pope Leo X | Patrons rewarded the scholars who honored them. | Leo X – Musurus: "patron of" | Infobox for each node after its card is answered: the person's dates and the reason text from the table, plus "Born on Crete" for Musurus, Kallierges, and Vlastos. **Provenance:** All contributions and dates from Part Two of this chapter (sections "Marcus Musurus," "Aldus Manutius," and "Aldine Editions"), checked against the Wikipedia articles for each person and for "Aldine Press." Life dates for Griffo, Kallierges, and Vlastos are approximate or uncertain; the sim shows them with "about" or "active." **Rules:** Cards appear in the order listed. Each card has one scored attempt; after a wrong first choice the learner may keep choosing until correct, but only the first choice is scored. A link is drawn only when its card is answered correctly (on any attempt), so the finished network has 8 links. Score is 0 to 10; mastery is score >= 8. The Crete question is scored separately: correct if the answer is 3. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads card 1 and chooses a person. 2. Feedback appears; when the choice is right, the link is drawn and the person's node shows its role. 3. The learner continues through card 10, watching the network grow around Aldus, with a separate pair, Kallierges and Vlastos, beside it. 4. The learner answers the Crete question. 5. The learner should notice that Aldus's name stands on the books, but at least seven other people made them possible, and that Cretans appear both inside his circle and in a rival press. **Feedback:** Correct: "Correct: [reason]." Incorrect: "Not [chosen person]. Think about which job this is: editing, publishing, type cutting, financing, teaching, writing, or patronage." After card 10: if score >= 8, "You can take a famous name apart into the team behind it."; otherwise, "Look again at cards 1, 3, and 6: Aldus did not do them." Crete question, correct: "Yes: Musurus, Kallierges, and Vlastos were Cretans."; incorrect: "Three: Musurus, Kallierges, and Vlastos." A Try Again option resets the cards. **Starting State:** Ten unconnected nodes, card 1, and the question "Who did this job?" **Chapter Anchors:** Plato 1513, edited by Musurus and dedicated to Leo X; Musurus to Rome 1516; Aldus's octavos from 1501; Griffo cut the italic; Torresani partner and father-in-law; Lascaris taught Musurus; Kallierges and Vlastos printed the *Etymologicum Magnum* in 1499; Erasmus in Aldus's house in 1508; Bembo edited Petrarch and Dante; ten people; three born on Crete; mastery 8 of 10.
